name: Junwen Lou
tagline: Machine Learning · Artificial Intelligence · Data Science
bio: My research interests broadly lie in machine learning, artificial intelligence, and data science.

I am interested in how learning algorithms can extract useful knowledge from data and support reliable decisions in real-world applications. My current experience includes time-series analysis, natural language processing, and model evaluation.
I also build software and data applications, with experience in backend development and data infrastructure.

sections.research:
Research Interests

My interests span machine learning, artificial intelligence, and data science, with an emphasis on learning from data and building useful, reliable systems.

Machine Learning

I am interested in learning algorithms, data representations, and how models generalize beyond the data used to train them.

Artificial Intelligence

I am interested in intelligent systems that can interpret information and support decision-making in practical settings.

Data Science & Applications

I am interested in turning complex data into useful insights. My current experience includes time-series analysis, natural language processing, and financial data applications.

For individual papers and manuscripts, see Publications ↗.

publications.title: Auditing Weakly Supervised Cryptocurrency Risk-State Learning: When Label Fit, Stability, and Semantics Disagree
publications.authors: Lou, J., Zhang, F., & Tian, S.
publications.detail_html:
Auditing Weakly Supervised Cryptocurrency Risk-State Learning: When Label Fit, Stability, and Semantics Disagree

Lou, J., Zhang, F., & Tian, S.

Manuscript

A three-axis audit of proxy-label agreement, temporal stability, and ex-post risk semantics using hourly data for five cryptocurrencies. Stronger label fit need not imply better risk stratification; the findings depend on the drawdown information encoded in the labels.

Research details
  • Temporal-model benchmarks on Bitcoin and Ethereum, with Transformer- and PatchTST-style stress tests on Bitcoin.
  • Baseline comparisons, ablations, label-design controls, and block-bootstrap analysis.
  • A Semantic Orientation Ratio to diagnose proxy-label misalignment, including XRP as a boundary case and explicit limits on general model ranking.

First author: study design, implementation, experiments, and manuscript preparation.
